papers.title: Deconstructing Guidance: A Semantic Hierarchy for Precise Diffusion Model Editing (Prism-Edit)

date.version: ICLR 2026 official conference PDF; precise initial submission date not verified

papers.status: ICLR 2026 conference paper; acceptance verified in official proceedings; reviews not read
sections_read: Main §§1–6, PDF pp1–10
Appendix A Gaussian bounds/proofs p13
Appendix B algorithms and integration pp14–15
Appendix C.1–C.10 experiments/ablations pp15–29
Appendix D disclosure p29; references scanned, not audited
papers.model: SD v1.5, SD3, FLUX.1 stated in §5; quantitative conventional-baseline integration primarily SD1.x; no inference run here
papers.task_data: Source-image editing: object/attribute/background/style; Wild-TI2I object/background split and ImageNet-R-TI2I (evaluated counts not stated in read text), CycleGAN tasks; COCO person probe ablation n=50; CUB bird→wooden carving n=100; DiffEdit comparison n=30
papers.permissions_reference: White-box noise/guidance access; source image and source/target conditioning (source can be null); inversion/source trajectory; optional source-latent blending. Does not require healthy model weights or a second clean donor image. GT-box variant is separately privileged.
papers.mechanism: Same x_t, source/target conditional noise difference; early probe t∈[900,800], averaged magnitude z-score semantic map; dynamic per-step guidance binarization and region-specific strength; optional static mask/source-latent blending. Thresholds fixed per baseline, not automatically selected per instance. Tweedie relates noise difference to posterior-mean shift; local-Gaussian bounds additionally assumed.
strong_baselines: DDIM/DDPM inversion, P2P, PnP, LEDITS++ with/without Prism modulation
RF-Inversion and Stable Flow for cross-model qualitative integration
DiffEdit n=30 subset; GT bounding-box preservation reference n=100

findings.anchor: Appendix C.5, Table C.2, PDF p21
findings.claim: Wild-background PnP→PnP+Prism: CLIP 0.3151→0.3200, DINO/SSIM 1.2240→1.7555. Counts for this split not given; ratio is not an all-facts success metric.
Wild-object DDIM: SSIM 0.4588→0.6942 but CLIP 0.3101→0.2997; PnP: SSIM 0.5554→0.6952 but CLIP 0.2995→0.2929. Shows trade-off, not uniform superiority.
COCO person n=50 seed=0: probe [900,800] coverage 0.9619, IoU 0.2651; later windows sometimes higher IoU. Probe selected empirically for coverage.

findings.anchor: Table C.6 p28; Figure C.13 p29 rendered
findings.claim: CUB n=100: Dynamic CLIP/SSIM 0.2393/0.6792; +Static 0.2132/0.6896; +GT box 0.2264/0.6859. Static protects more while reducing target alignment.

Mean-shift identity and Gaussian bounds do not by themselves prove that foreground always has stronger guidance or that masking universally preserves facts. Uniform images weaken separation; texture-rich background can be confused with object structure.

papers.closest_overlap: Directly covers interpretable guidance decomposition→instance-local, time-varying edit control→object/background preservation, including optional conservative protection. Generic diagnosis-guided low-side-effect editing and being model-agnostic are already claimed. Remaining candidate must predict conditional identity/relation effects or untried interventions rather than add another threshold.
limitations: Magnitude≈semantic-role interpretation has assumptions and empirical, architecture-dependent thresholds; it is not a universal causal localization guarantee.
DINO(object)/SSIM(background) can grow from background damage and is appropriate only with separate target checks for intended background change; not arbitrary protected-fact fidelity.
Main benchmark denominators and split construction detail insufficient for exact reaggregation in read PDF.
Latent equality outside a mask does not automatically imply pixel/semantic equality after coupled decoding; paper's strongest deterministic language should not be reused unqualified.
No matched-query black-box trial/beam baseline or held-out intervention-response prediction reported in read sections.

Conditional iterative refinement at steps 0/10/20 thresholds 0.05/0.5/0.8, max20 updates; ordinary guidance stops after first25 of50 denoising steps.
strong_baselines: Vanilla SD, StructureDiffusion, Composable Diffusion
P2P attention reweighting on 20 prompts/subset in appendix; original P2P replacement/refinement excluded because prompt meaning changes
No-Gaussian/no-refinement/all50-step ablations

findings.claim: BLIP-caption/CLIP text-text similarity A&E 0.806/0.830/0.811 vs SD 0.767/0.793/0.765 across three subsets. Nominal 276×64 images/method; NSFW-black outputs omitted without final retained denominator.
User preference 90.70%/77.64%/77.16%, n=65 respondents over sampled image sets. This is preference share, not per-image semantic success rate.
40 complex prompts×64 seeds: CLIP image-text 0.351 vs SD0.338 and StructureDiffusion0.336; no exact per-relation protected-fact rate.
A high attention patch can represent only a fragment while whole object is absent. Late latent updates add artifacts with little semantic improvement; early stopping is already baseline behavior.

papers.closest_overlap: Already performs diagnose worst subject→adaptive latent correction→final semantic evaluation, with explicit early stopping and multiple subject constraints. Choosing weak tokens and only early timesteps is not a new contribution.
limitations: Cross-attention localization and final object existence can disagree; optimized attention is not independent validation.
No strong constraint that other correct relations/identities survive; source layout can change substantially while fixing neglect.
Training-distribution/model-capacity limitations, unnatural co-occurrence, complex relations remain.
Runtime depends on adaptive refinement: author A100 ~9.7–15.4 s vs SD5.6 s; no same-budget repeated-sampling comparison, not local timing.

sections_read: Main §§1–7 pp1–9
Appendix A–G pp11–21, especially experimental config pp12–15 and limitations pp15–19
Key ablation plot/figure page20 rendered
papers.model: SD1.5 for matched-method quantitative experiments; SDXL for high-quality TEdBench comparison, Imagic+Imagen curated source outputs as different-backbone reference
papers.task_data: CelebA100 initially free of5 attributes; choose3 gives10 combinations×10 fixed seeds=10,000 images per method/hyperparameter, >1M overall. TEdBench100, revisedTEdBench++120; COCO segmentation4983images/29307objects; reconstruction100 COCO images.
papers.permissions_reference: Original image plus one or multiple edit concepts; white-box noise/cross-attention; invert image and reuse corrected stochastic noise. No source caption needed by default, no separate clean donor/weight tuning. Optional user masks are an additional permission.
papers.mechanism: Invert second-order SDE-DPM-Solver++ using stored noise corrections for exact latent reconstruction; per-concept signed guidance; each guidance masked by intersection of cross-attention and noise-difference quantile masks; sum concepts with independently selected scale/threshold. Per-step mask implicitly limits interference.
strong_baselines: Edit-friendly DDPM, DiffEdit, SDEdit, DDIM inversion, Pix2Pix-Zero, Imagic on SD1.5 with hyperparameter sweeps
For TEdBench: Imagic SD1.5; Imagic Imagen curated results vs SDXL explicitly different model/reference regime
Without semantic grounding; cross-attention-only/noise-only masks; CLIPSeg segmentation reference

findings.anchor: §6.1 p7, Appendix C.3 pp13–14, Figure5 p7/Figure18 p20
findings.claim: 10,000 images/method/hyperparameter: CLIP vs LPIPS trade-off favors LEDITS++; CLIP calculated separately for each3 attributes then mean. Plot-level trend, no invented exact coordinates. Spatial grounding ablation retains alignment but worsens preservation.

TEdBench++ n120: SD1.5 LEDITS SR0.79 LPIPS0.30 vs Imagic0.58/0.57; SDXL LEDITS0.87/0.34. SR from humans; LPIPS restricted to jointly successful edits. Results are hand-selected best of72 LEDITS outputs/case vs108 Imagic outputs/case; not one-shot or equal-query.
Zero reconstruction RMSE is in64×64 latent space over100 COCO images because VAE already induces pixel error. Timing100 A100 runs excludes I/O; not an end-to-end experiment budget guarantee.

Background/composition protection can change identity inside edited region; generic prompt, seed, wrong mask and base-model incapacity cause failure. Repeated same-class objects may require user masks. Reflections can be intentionally changed for coherent editing.

papers.closest_overlap: Already explicitly supports multiple simultaneous, individually grounded edits with minimized mutual interference and evaluates target-alignment/preservation trade-offs; 'multi-fact+local' is not enough. Per-attribute mean is weaker than all-facts success and preserving unchanged relations, but changing evaluation alone is not a method.
limitations: Perfect inversion is latent reconstruction, not guaranteed exact decoded original image.
TEdBench best-of-grid results include substantial selection cost and possible curator dependence; same budget must be re-established.
COCO mask quality uses GT bounding-box-size-derived threshold, so not fully unprivileged online localization.
No proof that additive guidance has additive semantic outcomes or no conditional interactions; masks can preserve background yet alter identity.

findings.anchor: Appendix pp12–13, Eq18, Tables1/5; full judge prompt pp17–19
findings.claim: ESER prose means source absent plus meaningful regional change; classifier maps NEITHER old nor target to absent, so this is not target success. Eq18 printed1−success_count/N conflicts with prose and ↑ direction; rendered confirms actual PDF, not extractor artifact. Some stated248-case percentages cannot be reproduced as rounded integer counts; raw aggregation needed, no cause inferred.

Background PSNR uses MSE of complete masked images, including zeroed foreground pixels; metric scales with mask area. LPIPS compares masked images. Neither certifies protected object attributes or relations.

papers.closest_overlap: Most direct near-neighbor of instance-specific controlled contrast→map→time×space×block intervention→multi-object edit and unrelated-content preservation. Source/target union already appears in P2P, but PC-Edit readout and same-step block sequencing are especially close. A task change to natural correction alone does not establish methodological novelty.
limitations: Only FLUX.1-dev and addition/replacement; no demonstrated conditional identity-vs-relation classification of shared connection.
No all-required-facts correctness endpoint; Qwen2.5-VL7B evaluator not calibrated against reported human outcome labels.
Block/step choices analyzed on benchmark; no held-out tuning split identified in read paper.
No query-matched direct black-box search/beam or held-out operation-effect prediction. Factual gaps above limit result strength but do not erase prior-art overlap.
